perf(patches): read signed files in 1 MiB pieces, the dyld cache uncached

cs_native4k_prepare reads the whole signed range of a file with 16K
page hashes before its signature is published. For the 3 GB dyld
shared cache that happens in launchd at every boot, and the cached
16 KiB reads filled the page cache: on the TB128FU free memory went
from 3.4 GB to 170 MB in the 42 s before the first daemon started, and
those daemons then started under memory pressure.

Read 1 MiB per vn_rdwr and use IO_NOCACHE for files above 32 MiB
(executables are faulted in right after their signature is added and
stay cached). Export the time spent in the reads and in the hashing
and the bytes read (cs_native4k_read_ticks, cs_native4k_hash_ticks,
cs_native4k_bytes) so a board can show what the boot pays.

TB128FU: free memory stays at 3.3 GB through the stall and the first
frame moved from 96 s to 86 s. The counters show 3141 MiB in 53 files,
28.9 s in the reads and 11.0 s hashing: the stall itself is bound by
the storage driver, so larger reads alone do not shorten it.

fix(patches): create /private/var/ngpu itself for the GPU addon

native_gpu_addon_parents starts its mkdir walk after
"/private/var/ngpu/", so it creates the directories below ngpu but
never ngpu. A Data seed that never had add-gpu-plugin-data.py applied
has no ngpu, every file of the payload's addon then fails with ENOENT
and the overlay mounts fail too, although make-gpu-addon.py says the
kernel creates missing directories. Start the walk at the slash after
ngpu so ngpu is created first (EEXIST when it is there).

Seen on the TB128FU (skip-setup seed without the plugin data):
files=9 written=0 failed=9 error=2, mounts 1.2/1.2; with the fix
written=9 and both mounts 5.0, the Metal plugin loads in backboardd.

ci(macos): publish only redacted text logs

The workflow is a build check. Kernels are linked against Apple's
kernelcache, payloads carry the platform seed and Apple content, and
userdata holds Apple's disk images, so none of them may be uploaded to a
public repository.

- Remove the kernel, payload and userdata uploads and the
  upload_userdata input.
- Upload only *.log files of the build, on success and failure, for 7
  days, after replacing the chip ID, the trust cache and Data seed URLs
  and signed URLs with ***, and skipping binary files.
- Write a step summary with the result of each build step.

ci(macos): rewrite the macOS build workflow

- Pin the runner to macos-26 and select Xcode by input (default 26.6)
  instead of the moving macos-latest label.
- Pass the workflow token to the kernel build so the DriverKit header
  listing is not rate limited.
- Install lld (no longer part of the llvm formula; the payload links
  the panic screen with ld.lld) and keep Homebrew LLVM off PATH, as on
  the development machines.
- Key the concurrency group on ref, device repository, device ref and
  defconfig, and stop cancelling running builds.
- Check the inputs, the defconfig, the Xcode path and the platform seed
  secret before installing or building anything.
- Read the trust cache and Data seed URLs from the event payload and
  mask them, so they do not appear in public logs.
- Drop the explicit fetch; the build step fetches the references it
  needs and no longer rewrites the device unixnu.lock.
- Let seed-data-grow.py find its submodule and build directory.
- Default to the kernel step and offer kernel plus payload without the
  userdata image.
- Upload the logs on failure, name artifacts per board and attempt,
  leave the skip-setup seed copy out of the payload artifact and store
  userdata uncompressed.
- Pin the actions to commits of their Node 24 releases and run steps
  with bash -eo pipefail.

feat(payload): keep the entry probe's timed reset from the board file

The payload ran patch-xnu-entry-probe.py only for panic_screen, always
with --no-reset. [payload] entry_probe_reset_delay now keeps the reset
(--reset-delay), and entry_probe_reset_after, _in, _occurrence and
_before move it after a given call (--reset-after, --in, --occurrence,
--reset-before), with or without the panic screen. Before the kernel
can draw, a reboot after the delay is the only sign that it got that
far. Without the new keys the call is unchanged.

[payload] skip_setup_args (optional) is passed to skip_setup_tool after

seed-data-skip-setup.py --no-auto-dim also sets SBDisableAutoDim,

fix(gpu): let Turnip bind host-import images at any offset

Turnip asked a dedicated allocation of every image made for external
memory, so an image over a no-copy buffer's host pages could not be
bound inside the buffer's import and each such texture fell back to a
shadow image copied in and out per pass. Ask it only for handle types
that carry per-image metadata, as the host-allocation format query
already reports.

into owner-data-volume.h next to the Data volume UUID and rebuilds

default.

NativeSandboxGrantProcess becomes a comma-separated list of process

feat(patches): copy the staged system apps into the data volume

The deletable system apps (Weather, Notes, Calendar and the rest) ship in
the OS volume's /private/var/staged_system_apps; a restore copies them
into Data, where the first-boot data migration installs them. The owner
Data mount hides that directory, so the apps and their widgets were
missing. With boot argument sheng-staged-apps=1 the kernel copies it once,
before launchd starts, through the vnode the Data mount covers, owned by
mobile (installcoordinationd moves the bundles as mobile). The walk is
iterative and every file is synced; /private/var/db/.sheng-staged-apps
marks a complete copy.

The payload passes --persistent-data to the ADT tool for boards that set
[payload.adt] persistent_data.

feat(payload): replace the default wallpaper's heic images with png

PosterBoard renders the iPad7,1 variant of wallpaper 7570, a layered
animation whose two HEIC images ImageIO cannot decode without a hardware
HEVC decoder, so the wallpaper stayed black.

scripts/make-wallpaper-overlay.py converts both images to 2732 pixel PNG
and points a copy of main.caml at them. make-gpu-addon.py --wallpaper
packs that directory into the addon. The kernel now creates missing
directories below /private/var/ngpu while it writes the addon, and
mounts /private/var/ngpu/wallpaper as a read-only union over the
animation's directory.

fix(payload): pass the text fixups after the ipad identity flag

The text fixup loop landed inside the ipad_identity condition, between
the if and its body, which leaves payload.py unparsable. Move it after
the --ipad-identity append.

feat(payload): pass signed-text fixups in the device tree

A board lists its fixups of signed file text in board.toml [payload]
text_fixups. The payload passes them to the ADT tool, which stores them
NUL-separated in /chosen/text-fixups, so they take no space on the
1000-byte command line. The kernel reads that table before the
text-fixup0..7 boot arguments and now holds up to 32 fixups.

feat(boot): accept a packed ramdisk of up to 1 TiB

The native sparse block driver keeps only the nonzero pages, so the
logical size is bounded by the format and not by memory. A dense
expansion still has to fit the owned window, which the loader checks.
The packer reads only the data regions of a sparse image and gives a
disk above 2 GiB an identity over its size and nonzero pages.

fix(vm): map GPU-written imports non-coherent and skip their per-submission cache work

Imports the GPU writes (render targets) are mapped non-cacheable instead of
write-back inner-shareable: the GPU stopped inside its end-of-pass cache clean
when system memory passes wrote them coherently. The owner's CPU does not touch
their pixels while the GPU owns them, so they were cleaned and invalidated at
map time and need no maintenance on every submission (about 60 ms per frame).
Read-only imports stay coherent.

fix(gmu): keep IFPC off until its restore list and fenced writes exist

fix(memory): hold imported pages through a memory entry

Core Animation unmaps an image's Shmem once its no-copy buffer is
released, which can come before the runtime frees the import. The
render thread of backboardd then stayed in vm_deallocate while the
import still had the pages wired by its UPL, and the desktop froze.

An import of user memory now asks for kIOMemoryPersistent, so the
descriptor keeps a memory entry and with it a reference on the VM
object; the owner's unmap leaves the object to the import until it
completes. A range no memory entry can be made of is imported as
before. Two counters tell the cases apart.

feat(userclient): record live imports and refused frees

A render server thread waited inside vm_deallocate for minutes on
int-233 and int-234. To tell whether an import of user pages is still
held over that range, the client now keeps the count of live imports,
the frees of an import it refused with the last status, and the eight
newest imports (address, owner pid, bytes, handle, state).

fix(vm): raise the GPU object limits to 4096

The shared VM mapping table held 1024 objects. int-237 filled it twice
(BoMap refused with kIOReturnNoResources at objects=1024): Turnip turned
the refusal into VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY inside a command stream
reservation it does not check, and backboardd crashed writing through a
NULL stream pointer; the other run froze with the same refusals.

Raise the VM table, the per-client entry table and the per-client view
cache to 4096, and record per client slot the live objects, their peak,
refused BoAllocs and the window's highest mapped end
(native_adreno_client_stats).

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ci5sg8z8jkQHR4QoXMBqfY

fix(userclient): serve metal clients beside the render server

- Four client windows: the render server keeps 1 GiB, and the
  wallpaper, icon and widget processes share the rest of the aperture
  (170 MiB each).
- A client that owns no queue range yet is no longer refused by
  setScope, held up in close or waited on in releaseAll because the
  render server has jobs in flight in the default range 0 (int-200).
  New regression block in the user-client host test.
- BoCpuUnmap keeps the shared CPU view while another mapping lease of
  the same BO is held; dropping it unmapped the other holder's pages
  and crashed the render server in vkCmdCopyBuffer (int-177).
- Diagnostics: the reason the latest mount failed, mappings that fall
  outside a client window, a text row per non-render-server process
  and a name for the mailbox poller thread.

perf(present): run the scanout thread at user-interactive priority

The thread that copies each frame to the screen shared the default priority with launching apps' threads and waited behind them; frame intervals above 40 ms at the 90th percentile dropped by about 5 ms.

recent_commits.message:
perf(present): run the scanout thread at user-interactive priority

The thread that copies each frame to the screen shared the default priority with launching apps' threads and waited behind them; frame intervals above 40 ms at the 90th percentile dropped by about 5 ms.

fix(plugin): render in system memory again

Revert the nobin setting: with GPU-written imports mapped non-coherent the system
memory passes no longer stall, and they take about 10 ms of GPU time per frame
against about 17 ms for tile memory passes without binning.

fix(plugin): render without hardware binning

Every Metal process now starts Turnip with TU_DEBUG=nobin,nocb. A binned pass
hands its visibility work to the BV thread, and with BV and BR waiting on each
other inside a pass the GPU stalled and the display froze. Without binning a
pass stays on BR and renders in tile memory; over two 7 minute runs of scripted
swipes no submission stalled.

fix(plugin): render in system memory without concurrent binning

Every Metal process now starts Turnip with TU_DEBUG=sysmem,nocb. In
GMEM passes, and with concurrent binning in system memory passes too,
the BV thread runs ahead of BR across passes; on this GPU the two
stopped waiting on each other inside an IB (GPU idle, BR at the start of
the submission, BV near its end), which froze the display. With both
off no submission stalled over long manual sessions.

fix(frontend): make textures on two-plane IOSurfaces

Widget snapshots are drawn into the render server's two-plane RGB
surfaces ('_RB4') as RGB8_444_2P textures. The frontend imported every
surface plane as a single-plane texture, so the runtime refused them
and the widgets stayed white. Surfaces with two planes now go through
a new bridge call that passes the surface's format, size and second
plane, and the runtime accepts '_RB4' as an 8-bit 4:4:4 surface. The
SR row also prints the surface format in hex.

feat(frontend): report why a surface texture was refused

The texture status row counted refused IOSurface textures but not the
check that refused them. An SR row now shows the last refusal's step,
the surface's pixel format, plane, plane offset, row bytes and
allocation, and the descriptor's size and pixel format.

feat(display): retire a GPU-copied swap when the client takes it

The compositor renders the next frame only after the current swap
retires. Retiring after the hand-off copy finished serialized render
and copy. The swap now retires as soon as the GPU client accepts the
frame; the next frame is still held until the copy completes.
sheng-early-retire=0 restores retirement after the copy.

The compositor renders the next frame only after the current swap

and copy. The swap now retires as soon as the GPU client accepts the

sheng-early-retire=0 restores retirement after the copy.

feat(display): report one fixed refresh rate on request

The panel runs at one rate, but the reported maximum refresh interval
stays at the original 1/24 s, so the render server sees a 24 to 144 Hz
range and may pace frames anywhere in it. With sheng-vsync-fixed=1 the
maximum interval equals the minimum.

feat(display): report the panel refresh rate

The render server paces its display timer by displayMinRefreshInterval
in IOMFBDisplayRefresh, and without that property it keeps its own
1/60 s heartbeat. Nothing in the original family publishes it (its
platform subclass does), and the generic slot 301 fixes the minimum at
1/60 s. With sheng-vsync=<Hz> the display now overrides slot 301
(getRefreshAttributes) with the panel's rate and calls the original
setDisplayRefreshProperties before registerService. int-211 showed
frames 8 to 9 ms apart at 144 Hz.

The same boot argument starts a work-loop timer that sends the
family's original vsync message (type 5) while a client has vsync
notifications enabled. The render server on this target uses its own
display timer and never registers, so the timer stays idle for now.

fix(gop): re-kick the swap queue after each retirement

A waiting swap is offered at once instead of on the next event.

feat(gop): add a swap stage timeline hook

Per-stage timestamps of each swap for offline frame timing analysis.

fix(gop): report the firmware-lit panel as powered and keep several swaps pending

Several validated swaps may now wait in the queue.

Current state: the CPU and GPU scanout paths work. The GOP scanout has no vblank interrupt; with `sheng-vsync=<Hz>` a work-loop timer sends the original family's vsync message to the compositor.

native_ram_block_gpu_addon() returns the bytes of the addon the loader
recorded at /chosen/memory-map/GpuAddon, bounds checked against the
physical memory and capped at 64 MiB, for the kernel's boot-time addon

fix(ram): read a large disk from its seed before the store attaches

APFS probes the disk for its volume UUID long before the kernel asks
for the Data volume, which is what attaches the store. Reads are served
from the seed until then, and writes wait.

feat(ram): keep only the nonzero pages of a seed above 2 GiB

SeedDisk holds the nonzero pages of a large seed sorted by index, so
a disk of hundreds of GiB costs memory in proportion to its content.
Such a disk has no volatile mode and needs the store open read-write.
Its identity hashes the size and the nonzero pages with their index.

feat(ram): accept sheng-data-reset=2 as a reset

Value 2 also asks the board to show the Setup page on that boot.

feat(ram): serve the data disk straight from the store window

Changed pages are read from and written to UFS and none are kept in
RAM, which frees about 2 GiB of memory for the system.

feat(ram): name the overlay reset argument sheng-data-reset

sheng-data-reset=1 drops the stored overlay and starts from the seed.

feat(ufs): size the end-of-disk reserve with sheng-log-reserve

The Data store ends below a reserve at the end of userdata instead of
a quarter of the partition. The log and its export region sit inside
the reserve (default 1024 MiB). The log is refused when the reserve is
smaller than they need.

fix(live): observe the context only on whole-verification updates

Updates between the whole-verification ones (every 64th) no longer read
the context image and faults around the stores. A map of invalid leaves
skips TLB invalidation, as Linux io-pgtable does. An unmap there syncs
its ASID with ArmSmmu4KSyncContextTlb at the offset the last whole
update observed.

fix(streams): observe owned routes without the all-slot scan

ArmSmmu4KObserveOwnedStreams reads only the global fault policy, the
enabled context image and the owned SMR/S2CR pairs, a fixed count
whatever the SMMU size. The full ArmSmmu4KObserveStreams scan stays for
periodic audits.

commits.message:
perf(config): start only the boot core and the five big cores

The two other little cores (A510) were handed work as often as a big core and ran it several times slower. The payload now lists the boot core plus the A715, A710 and X3 cores.

perf(sched): keep the boot core busy so work lands on the big cores

The scheduler sees six equal cores and hands work to the lowest idle core number first, which is the little A510 boot core. A lowest-priority thread bound to that core keeps it occupied while any big core is idle and yields to real work when none is. Compositing in the heavy swipe scenes went from a 21 ms to a 16 ms median frame interval (40 to 55 fps). sheng-cpu0-park=0 turns it off.

The profile rows also show, per busy process, how its samples spread over the cores.

fix(probe): remove the merge markers left in the swipe script

The previous commit carried unresolved merge markers. The scripted run keeps the Control
Center, Notification Center and app open and close scenes, the tracking ids within the
panel's range, and a scripted contact the panel's empty frames cannot lift.

feat(probe): script Control Center, Notification Center and app open and close in the swipe run

The scripted run now pulls down Control Center and Notification Center and opens and
closes the Clock app before the page swipes, and logs the time range of each scene in a
[swipe2] row. Empty frames from the panel no longer lift the scripted contact.

feat(board): add the Install and boot menu entry

A second boot menu entry, behind a confirmation, erases the Data seed's persistent store and boots with or without the Hello pages (sheng-data-reset=1 or 2).

chore(touch): update the NativeNovatekTouch pointer

Brings in finger tracking through rests, panel drift and close contacts, with optimal finger-to-blob matching.

fix(backlight): stop the GENI TX watermark interrupt storm

Turn the level TX watermark off in the interrupt handler and enable only the M_IRQ bits the I2C core handles, so the line drops once the status is read. Log interrupts with an empty status and the last status seen.
fix(brightness): carry brightness requests to the work loop on a timer and log the request path
fix(brightness): hand brightness requests to the work loop without blocking the caller
fix(brightness): let backboardd set the backlight's brightness and fade period
fix(touch): match fingers to blobs by least total distance from their predicted positions

fix(touch): track the panel's drift and keep the strongest maxima

The reference was taken once at startup, so the raw values drifted until faint maxima appeared all over the panel. They filled the peak table in scan order and a finger found after them was dropped, which broke multi-finger touch. The reference now follows the panel in frames without a finger, and a full table gives up its weakest maximum for a stronger one. New counters report the largest number of maxima in a frame, the overflowing frames and the frames that moved the reference.

fix(touch): smooth positions with an adaptive filter instead of a rest lock

A slow finger was held at rest until it was 20 px away and then jumped there, so slow movements and pauses reached SpringBoard as stops and jumps. Positions now go through a low-pass filter whose cutoff rises with the finger's speed: a still finger keeps its place through the centroid noise and a moving one is followed every frame. The log counters report the steps left after smoothing.
fix(touch): fold a finger's second maximum into its stronger one

fix(touch): lock a resting finger and weigh only the blob's core

The centroid now weighs nodes above 30% of the blob's peak, so fringe
nodes that come and go with noise no longer move it. A resting finger is
locked until it moves 20 px away, a moving one locks again once its
last six positions span less than that, and frames below the down
threshold (a finger lifting off) leave the position unchanged. The core
counts rests and unlocks.

fix(touch): hold a finger through a few frames without its blob

A tracked finger that matches no blob is kept and reported at its last
position for up to three frames before it counts as lifted, so a single
weak or missing frame no longer ends a swipe. The core counts bridged
gaps, lifts by miss reason and frames by type.

fix(touch): hold a resting finger's position with a fuzz filter

Every frame reported the raw centroid, whose noise made a resting finger
look like it was still moving. iPadOS opens the app switcher only when a
swipe up pauses with near-zero velocity, so the gesture always went
home.

Each axis now passes through a fuzz filter: steps within half the fuzz
(0.5 mm) keep the reported position, steps up to twice the fuzz are
blended in, larger ones pass. Tracking still uses the raw position. The
core also counts the raw step size of resting and slow contacts, so the
fuzz can be checked against the panel's real noise.
